growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): to 120 dm.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs or trees.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: deciduous.

traits.spines.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): thorns on the twigs, few to many.

traits.spine_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): thorns 0.7-1 cm, the stout lateral ones to 2.4 cm.

traits.bark_colour.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: bark grey-brown.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves lustrous dark green above, paler beneath; sRGB by eye.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaf a single blade.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade with 1-3 lobes a side, the sinuses usually deep.

traits.division_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): lobes along the midrib.

traits.leaf_lobes.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 1-3 lobes a side and the end one: 3 to 7.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade 1.2-5.5 cm.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petiole slender, 1-3 cm.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade ovate to deltate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): apex acute.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): margins weakly and often few-toothed at the lobe tips.

traits.anther_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): anthers pink-purple; sRGB by eye.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): style 1 (one-seeded, hence monogyna).

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pomes.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pomes 6-11 mm across.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pomes usually dark red, sometimes bright; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pomes orbicular to somewhat cylindric, 6-11 mm across; Wikipedia, Crataegus monogyna (read 2026-10-19): the haw small, oval, about 10 mm long. Between round and cylindric: ellipsoid.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowering April to May.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Crataegus monogyna var. monogyna (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruiting September to October.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a dense thorny small tree with small deeply lobed glossy leaves, sprays of white flowers with pink anthers and dark red haws.

allometry.note: 9.0 m tall at 25 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

traits.fruits_per_inflorescence.note: Wikipedia, Crataegus monogyna (read 2026-10-19): the haws develop in groups of two or three along the smaller branches, from corymbs of 5-15 flowers (FNA).
